nodes.role: Finds every engagement under the clients root: any folder holding the engagement's record (ledger.LEDGER_FILENAME), without descending into one. Reads each record's details for client, link, due, sender, firm, reminders and active. A folder holding only the workbook the tracker no longer reads (LEGACY_MANIFEST_FILENAME) and no record is terminal too and is listed as a legacy folder (LEGACY_FOLDER), never as an engagement. There is no registry file.
nodes.notes: Replaced engagements.yaml (decision 27): a hand-kept list a typo could silently skip a client from. Hidden/underscore folders and Prepared/Shared are skipped, depth is capped at MAX_DEPTH, a record the readers refuse is listed with its problem rather than dropped, and a root with no engagement at all is an error - that is a typo in the scheduled task, not an empty practice. mark_superseded(): an engagement another one was rolled forward from is inactive with its successor named - the rollover never writes to the prior, so the successor's details are the record. Engagement wraps EngagementInfo and delegates its fields rather than copying them. Decision 66: _same_folder() matches Rolled From by the client and engagement folder names when the absolute path no longer resolves. Decision 67: _prior_of() never compares an engagement with itself and matches the engagement sharing the most trailing names only when it is the only one; the walk lists a folder it could not read as a problem row, never a silence (decision 125 turned it into the positional _walk_root()/_walk_private()/_walk_household()/_walk_year(), and a folder it cannot list is the UNLISTED misfit). Decision 68: a Rolled From that matches nothing is a warning the engagement carries (ROLLED_FROM_UNMATCHED); a problem row is never the prior. Decision 104: discovery is by the journal, not by a workbook; engagement_from() reads the details and the rules through the store, catching ManifestError, LedgerError and StoreError - and, named by type, any other exception one synced record raises - into the problem, so one folder cannot end the pass inside discovery; a folder whose record carries no rules beside the legacy workbook is listed the same way as one with no record (an engagement created before decision 103 whose rules never reached the journal). Nothing imports such a folder, by the owner's word: it is set up again in the app. This is the one reader of LEGACY_MANIFEST_FILENAME in the package. It imports store and ledger (L1) from L3, which the layers allow. Decision 131: _prior_of() reads layout.shared_tail and layout.ROLLED_FROM_TAIL (moved there from _shared_tail/_TAIL_NAMES so the scaffold reads the same rule); _same_folder stays here because it resolves, which layer 0 must not.

nodes.role: Drafts the client chase email from a scanned engagement's record, or holds it for a person. Since decision 117 the letter has four stages (STAGES, stage_for(), stage_named()) chosen by how far today is from the Due Date, and the words of all four are here and nowhere else. Draft only - there is no SMTP anywhere in this module, and tests/test_layers.py pins that no module under the package imports a mail or network one.
nodes.notes: Validation notes are translated into plain client instructions, never quoted. Rows we have not read yet, and rows with no request folder, are held back for a person instead of being asked for. Each draft carries a fingerprint of its own text so an edited draft is never overwritten. A Partial row whose shortfall is a file we have not read is held back too. Reads the engagement's details from the record for client, link, due, sender and firm (manifest.load_engagement_info(); a folder with no record is a ReminderError naming the journal's file); keyword arguments are one-off overrides for the CLI. Decision 57: write_draft() raises DraftsEditedError rather than overwrite an edited NEW draft; the runner reports BOTH_DRAFTS_EDITED and writes nothing. Decision 62: EXTENSION_ASK names the row's own file types; --write preserves edits. Decision 76: count_needs_review() is still the folder's count less the working copies whose newest index row is filer.NOT_REQUESTED. An index it cannot read leaves every file counted. Decision 103: the draft is built from the record alone; a status only the record holds is what it counts. Decision 115: triage() returns a fourth list, held - a Failed row with no firm-side marker, or a Partial whose shortfall is a refused file, is ambiguous (AMBIGUOUS_HOLD) and one such row holds the whole draft: write_draft() raises ReminderHeldError (HELD_REFUSAL, naming every held row) before touching a file, the CLI prints HELD lines and --write exits 2, and SECTION_FAILED left SECTION_ORDER (unreachable from a pass; client_ask()'s Failed branch kept for an action a person may one day record). A firm-side marker on any outstanding status, Missing included, is the firm's (109's rule stated once). The draft is on the record: drafted_event() builds the ledger.DRAFTED event (asked identifiers, file and fingerprint; or held identifiers), draft_changed() says whether it differs from the last one (or is a new draft week's, when the caller passes the week), record_draft() writes it through store.record() under the caller's lock, last_draft_event() reads the newest (or the newest carrying a key). write_draft(changed_from=...) opens the header with CHANGED_HEADING / CHANGED_ADDED / CHANGED_REMOVED against the last event that carried asked, above the separator. HELD_SUMMARY is the one line the app shows, through api._vocab(). Decision 117: the draft escalates in four stages against the Due Date (STAGE_2_DAYS, STAGE_3_DAYS - constants, the owner's), each with its own subject, intro, deadline paragraph and close; the stage changes the words only - triage() still decides the recipients and the gate holds at every stage - and the sentences name the Due Date and the Filing Deadline and never the arithmetic between two dates a person may have moved. The stage rides in the header above the fingerprint line (STAGE_LINE, so an edit is still never overwritten) and in the DRAFTED event (STAGE_KEY), which draft_changed() compares as a fifth key, so a client who crossed a threshold gets this week's draft even when the asked set did not move; --stage and --today write another stage's or another day's letter. The final notice's phone sentence comes from settings.firm_phone() - the firm's, not the engagement's - and is dropped when that is blank. And the hold of decision 115 gained a second cause: a parked index row whose reason reasons.find() calls client-side, and whose shortlist in tracker/review.py names a request still asked for, holds that request (PARKED_HOLD, _parked_holds(), a call-time import of review), because a drop the rules refused at tier 2 never reaches a status and the draft would ask for a document the client knows they sent; draft_reminder() reads the rows itself and the API hands in the ones it has already read. It reads the SHORTLIST and not the row's Candidates cell: candidates are the requests that accepted the file, and a file refused before a word of it could be read - the locked PDF, the headline case - has none, so the draft and the review card now answer 'what does this parked file point at?' the same way. Decision 118: the letter is a structure before it is words. _compose_letter() builds a Letter (greeting, progress, intro, sections, drop lines and link, the deadline paragraph as runs, close, sign-off) and Letter.text() is the body the file carries, so the plain text, render_html()'s inline-styled body for the clipboard and the shape the app draws its preview from are three renderings of one thing and cannot say different things. The deadline paragraph is cut into runs by formatting the stage's own sentence with sentinels round the target, the filing deadline and the consequences sentence - never by searching the finished sentence for a date, which an engagement name could also contain. STAGE_COLOURS, HOLD_COLOUR, LETTER_INK name keys of page.PALETTE and STAGE_EMPHASIS says where each stage spends its colour and its weight; render_html() reads that table and the API ships it, so the letter, the clipboard and the card apply one ladder. render_html() is rendered on demand and never written to disk - the .txt stays what the pass writes. approved_event()/last_approved_event()/is_approved_this_week()/is_protected() are the approval a person makes in the app: until the next draft day the pass treats the approved file exactly as it treats one somebody edited (write_draft(approved_since=...) puts the regenerated draft in the .NEW file instead), and set_aside_other_draft() renames any draft standing beside it by SET_ASIDE_DRAFT_PATTERN rather than deleting it. Imports tracker.page at load time for esc() and the palette, which is L3 -> L0. An approval holds against every writer, not only the pass: is_approved_this_week(since=None) asks only whether this is the approved file, so the command line - a layer below the runner, and unable to learn the draft week - lands its --write draft beside an approved one rather than over it, and the pass, which knows the week, is the one caller that spends the approval. pasted_text() gives the letter between the header's rule and FOOTER_RULE: the staff-side footer write_draft() may add is the machine's note to the person, as the header is, and firm-side sentences must not be one paste from a client. DECISION 133 - THE REMINDER WAITS FOR THE SORT: unsorted_in_inbox() counts the distinct paths the filer's iter_drops, unfinished_drops and unreachable_drops (imported at call time, as the rest of this module reaches the filer) return for layout.inbox_of() of the return - its OWN household's inbox only; an inbox in another household that also feeds it (decision 132) is not read, a known limit. draft_reminder() stores it as ReminderDraft.unsorted, and is_held is now bool(held) or unsorted > 0, so the pass, the command line and the app hold alike and write_draft() refuses before touching a file; held stays the rows. held_refusal() says INBOX_HOLD when files wait, HELD_REFUSAL when rows hold, both joined by '; '; INBOX_HELD_SUMMARY is the app's line (api vocab inbox_held_line). A hold records a drafted event with held and no file, so the next pass that sorts the inbox drafts the same day. Decision 137 (L5): a recorded link that is not http(s) (records.link_problem) is left out of the letter and ReminderDraft.link_dropped says so (LINK_DROPPED), above the footer and on the CLI; saving one is refused by the manifest and the household writers. Decision 140: _parked_holds() asks reason.holds, not 'not firm_side'; a firm-side reason that holds (SHOWS_ITS_FORM_NUMBER) says CONFIRM_HOLD with the reason's firm note and no client ask, so neither the held line nor the draft ever says the client's file was wrong; a client-side hold keeps PARKED_HOLD word for word.

nodes.role: Triages the review queue: turns the evidence an index row kept - the rows handed to triage(), which since decision 100 the caller must read and pass - into a ranked shortlist of at most three requests a parked file might belong to, each with the one-line reason it is on the list. Layer 2 - it suggests, and it files nothing.
nodes.notes: Decision 83. triage(engagement_dir) returns one Triage per index row decided NEEDS_REVIEW, each holding the row and a tuple of Suggestion(identifier, reason, rank). It writes no artifact at all: no sidecar, no status, no move, no lock, and no client document is opened - the index's Evidence column is already the store, and a second one could disagree with it the moment somebody filed a row by hand. It reads the manifest and the index (read_index over the engagement folder, which since decision 102 answers from the store and moves nothing at all); a caller that already loaded either passes it in. rank sorts ascending as (identity, strength, catalog): identity is a slot reserved for a later step and constant today, strength is RULE_STRENGTH before PLACE_STRENGTH so a required keyword said deep outranks an any-keyword in a title - the way the router already weighs the two rules - and the manifest's own order breaks a tie as a tie. Evidence only: the request list's Missing/Received state is deliberately not a tiebreaker and never fills a shortlist (owner, 2026-09-18), because a nudge with nothing behind it is how a tired reviewer files the wrong document into the last open row. So a row whose evidence says nothing - matched no request, a scan whose name says nothing either, a record carrying only a refusal - gets an empty shortlist and keeps the router's own reason, and a row set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE is never suggested - it is NAMED instead (decision 116): Triage.set_aside carries each such row the evidence pointed at with its year's label, said in SET_ASIDE_NOTE on the review card and the Status Report, so the person who set it aside decides and the machine never files under it. Since decision 92 an unreadable scan whose name DOES carry a row's keyword arrives here with RULE_FILENAME evidence and is offered as 'A01 - the file name says W-2' at the bottom of the ranking: the one piece of evidence the client wrote rather than the form, so it starts a person reading and can never outrank a word the document itself said. A RULE_REFUSED entry is never a suggestion by itself; beside content evidence its cause is said in that suggestion's sentence, in the words reasons.py gives it. PLACE_WORDS is the one mapping from an evidence place to the words for it, so api._vocab() can expose it rather than the app typing a word of its own. Nothing below it imports it, and it imports neither runner, scheduling, settings nor api; genre and group are reserved for later steps. Decision 128 filled the rank's first slot, reserved for identity since C5: a row whose page confirmed one of the return's spellings (records.RULE_NAME evidence) ranks IDENTITY_AGREES and sorts above every keyword tier, and the sentence behind each suggestion says which of the three the name check answered. The name then stays OUT of the strength slot: it is on every candidate of the row and at the strongest tier there is, so counting it there too would give them all one minimum and leave the keyword tiers ordering nothing. A veto is told from a confirmation by reasons.NAMES_ANOTHER_RETURN.matches() - decision 121's one way to read a reason - because on a vetoed row the RULE_NAME evidence carries the OTHER return's spelling and a missed veto would say the page names this return's person; the other return's label is then read back off the row's own reason through records.as_pattern, anchored on the escaped spelling and greedy to the sentence's fixed tail so a return name holding a parenthesis is read whole, as filer.moved_to reads a path back off one: the spelling is the evidence and a label is not evidence of anything.

nodes.role: Builds a returning client's next-year request list from their prior engagement's record. Prior-year data always wins; the template may only fill blanks. The rows it builds are recorded into next year's engagement by manifest.create_engagement() - the API's rollover and this module's CLI both do that - and the offers and last year's unfiled files are reported once, in the reply and on the command line. Since decision 126 it also rolls a whole household: roll_household() takes the household's one open year (open_year_returns()), rolls every ReturnPlan into the target year one at a time and retires every open-year return nobody ticked with one details edit, answering with a HouseholdRollover of what rolled, what refused and what was retired.
nodes.notes: Years shift as a set so relative periods stay right. Counts learn from what arrived and never shrink. Override.NOT_APPLICABLE carries forward under its own origin (ORIGIN_NOT_APPLICABLE) with NOT_APPLICABLE_NOTE - last year's label and 'decide afresh' - printed by the CLI after the carried and new rows under PREVIOUS_NOT_APPLICABLE_HEADING and grouped by the app's returning-client page, never back in the active list (decision 116; decision 10 stands); Accepted does not, and neither does its reason. The CLI's form template comes from tracker.templates, so this module and tracker.api do not import each other. Derived year checks are left blank on the rolled rows; the shifted Period derives them again when the list is validated. Decision 67: a template row is the prior's row whatever its case, as validated() compares identifiers. Decision 69: roll_forward() refuses a target year not after the prior's. Decision 72: and one outside YEAR_MIN..YEAR_MAX, through manifest.check_tax_year(), as the wizard's box does. Decision 86: carry_engagement_info() carries the form the prior was cut from into next year's details - a returning client files the same return - and carries a blank as a blank. Decision 103: last year is read from the record (load_manifest() lays the keywords a filing taught over the row's typed ones), so a taught keyword reaches _carry() as a keyword like any other and lands in next year's list as an ordinary Any Keyword - the one moment a taught word becomes something typed, and a learned row would be invisible in the editor. Decision 104: the Carried Forward sheet is not written - the workbook it was written into is gone, and the writer is set aside outside the tree; an offer a person wants is added later in the app's editor. The prior year is read and never written. Decision 108: the command line takes page.tolerant_console() first (its report carries an arrow a cp1252 console cannot encode, and it used to die after the record was written and before the folders were made, with a second run refused), and does all of its work - create_engagement(), then scaffold_engagement() when asked - before it prints a line, so nothing about the report can leave a folder with a record and no scaffold. Decision 123: with_default_dates() lives here, beside the carry rule that clears the two dates, so both ways of building next year's engagement fill them - the command line wraps carry_engagement_info() in it (the form the prior recorded, else the one asked for, and the target year) and tracker.api imports it for create and rollover; the defaulting used to live in the API alone, and the command line's engagements came out with no Due Date at all. Decision 126: roll_household() is the household's loop and roll_forward() stays the primitive it calls, so one return still rolls on its own; each rolled return is created under its own lock by create_engagement() and a refusal on one (an existing target, the path limit through filer.refuse_a_path_past_the_limit(), a year not after the prior's) lands in HouseholdRollover.skipped with its sentence and undoes none of the others. A return that was ticked is never retired by the loop - rolled, its successor's Rolled From retires it; refused, it is still this year's work. The client's side is laid out once at the end (scaffold_household()), so the inbox README lists the new year's lists the day the firm rolls. The CLI carries both forms in one __main__, told apart by store.kind() - a household folder takes --year with --all or --only and prints ROLLED / NOT ROLLED / RETIRED, a return folder is the per-return form unchanged. Decision 137 (L5): carried_link() drops a household link that is not a web address with LINK_NOT_CARRIED (RolloverReport.link_dropped), rather than refusing the roll; the API carries it to the app.

nodes.role: Decides which single manifest row a dropped file belongs to. Evidence order: required keywords, then any-keywords/period, read off a text layer or off OCR (OCR routes on required keywords only). There is no third tier: a file name is never evidence for a filing (decision 92), and a document nothing could be read out of parks. The router knows no person (decision 128): whose document this is is asked by the household pass against the return's own people list, not here.
nodes.notes: Reads the document through content_check.extract() - the scanner's reading - and leaves its per-row verdicts among the engagement's verdicts in the store (content_check.ContentCache) keyed by content, so the scan finds them under the working copy's name. Every scan with no text layer is OCR'd, whatever its name says, and OCR text routes only on required keywords - an any-keyword match on OCR text is OCR_ONLY, a lead for a person, because a misread word is how a document lands under the wrong request. One PdfVerdictCache per file (or the caller's) so a PDF is parsed once, not once per row. The CLI (python -m tracker.router <engagement> <files>) says where each file would go and why, moving nothing. Extension alone never routes. A document matching one row's required keywords but failing its other rules is contested and blocks its own filing — misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it. When nothing routes, the reason is the most useful one available: a document whose content fits a row that refused the file (size floor, type, unreadable PDF) is reported as CONTESTED_PREFIX, and a file every row refused for the same reason carries that reason. A file name is read the same whole-token way a keyword is, run-together spelling and all (W2 for W-2), but only ever as evidence for a person. Eligibility is has_routing_rules(): keywords or a typed year; a year derived from Period only checks a document a keyword already matched. Decision 55, as decision 92 left it: a text layer extract() marked needs_ocr is no text at all, so a multi-page scan is read no further than a one-page one - and where 55 then filed it on its name, it now parks. Decision 58: no run-together fallback; the keyword pattern already reads a dash or space as optional. Decision 73: a row whose any-keywords all matched and whose year alone failed is remembered as a lead, and a file that would otherwise be parked with 'matched no request' is parked as 'looks like J01 (expected period not found ...)' with J01 as its candidate - the sentence a contested file gets, so the reminder asks the client about the period. A lead pre-empts no filing, unlike a required-keyword match, so the decision is exactly as it was; only the reason and the candidates improve. The Routing record and EVIDENCE_CONTENT live in tracker/records.py (decision 100) and are re-exported here for one release: the decision is a record, this module is the deciding. Decision 82: Routing.evidence_record is why, beside Routing.evidence, the tier the decision rested on - EVIDENCE_CONTENT or nothing, since decision 92 removed EVIDENCE_FILENAME (nothing rests on a name; content_check.RULE_FILENAME, the word an index row actually carries, is untouched and still produced). Keyed by candidate identifier: the content check's own Evidence tuple for a row that was read, _filename_evidence() for what the name said (a name is all title and has no page), and _refusal_evidence() for a tier-2 refusal, which travels as reasons.Reason.code rather than the sentence a person reads. _recorded_for() cuts it down to the identifiers the decision names, because every row considered leaves something behind and one index cell must not carry the whole manifest's workings. It decides nothing: every verdict is reached exactly as it was before there was a record. Decision 84: a blocked file - content fits a row, the same row's tier-2 rules refused the file - keeps the verdict's evidence beside the refusal in record, because the refusal alone says which rule said no and never which request the document looked like. The verdict was already read there to decide the file was blocked, so nothing is computed twice and no placement moves. Decision 117: a tier-2 refusal on a file nothing could be read out of - a locked PDF, an empty upload - is asked what its NAME says, exactly as an unreadable scan is, and the name's evidence is recorded beside the refusal for the person who has to open it (and for the reminder's hold, which reads the review shortlist). The decision does not move an inch: no candidate, the same reason, nothing filed on a name. Decision 92, the owner's (2026-09-18): A DOCUMENT NOBODY CAN READ IS FILED BY NOBODY. The by-name tier is gone - when no word of the file could be read (a scan with no text layer OCR could not rescue, an image-only PDF, an empty sheet) no row is a candidate, and the file parks with reasons.NO_READABLE_TEXT (router.UNREADABLE), which is deliberately not UNMATCHED: nothing was matched against anything, and the fix is OCR or a person, never another keyword. _filename_evidence() stays and is recorded on the parked row, so review.triage() offers the request the name points at at RULE_STRENGTH's weakest tier and the app's card and the Status Report show it - a place for a person to start reading, never a filing. _read() no longer skips OCR for a sensibly named scan: nothing is filed on a name, so OCR is the only thing that can still file one, and the scan whose name says W-2 is exactly the one whose content must be read (the _filename_hit shortcut went with the skip). The cost was stated and accepted: until Tesseract is installed every scanned PDF parks - twelve rows of the firm's own corpus moved from filing to parking, and two the name had been misfiling now park instead. Decision 93 (a row per issuer): an issuer row is an ordinary row carrying the entity's name in Required Keywords, and which row wins needed no new rule - a required keyword is the strongest tier and the generic K-1 row has none, so the issuer row takes the K-1 that names it. The one rule added is the park: when any row narrows the row that accepted a document (manifest.narrowing_rows over the rows this pass considers, so an issuer row set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE is nobody's issuer) and none of the narrowing rows matched, nothing is filed - reasons.ISSUER_NOT_NAMED, the narrowing rows named, shortlist led by the row that did accept it. Filing on the generic row would put two entities' K-1s in one folder; taking the row left over would be guessing by elimination. Decision 107: whether a page counts two forms as its own is content_check.own_forms(), the same reading the scanner's miss path makes; computed once in route_file() and handed to evaluate_rules() for the ordinary reading and to the split alike, so a page that prints two forms' own names never files on a third form it merely mentions (decision 94's rule, by construction); the forms are then taken in first-mention order (self_named_forms) for the filing order, and _multi_form() decides exactly as before. Decision 105: the split's verdicts are remembered too. _multi_form() takes route_file()'s keep closure and calls it for every row it files a copy under, with the second reading's verdict, after the ordinary reading has left its own refusal - the verdict the router files on is the one the scan must find, or the second copy fails validation on the next pass and the client is asked for a form they already sent. A page that parks keeps nothing new. Decision 128 gave route_file() a `reading` argument in place of `text`: the household pass reads each drop once (read_once()) and routes that one Extraction against every return it feeds, so a two-return household costs one reading rather than two, and from_ocr travels with it so decision 50's stricter rule still applies. Decision 127 changed no rule here: a photo arrives with from_ocr set, so decision 50's stricter reading applies to it unchanged, and route_file() only became two functions - itself, which makes the two refusals that must come before any reading (a cloud placeholder is never read, a Google stub is never a document) and then stamps Routing.seconds on whatever _decide() returns, and _decide(), which is the whole decision as it was. The seconds decide nothing; they let the pass name its slowest documents. Decision 137: route_file() parks a file past validators.MAX_READ_MB before any reading, with reasons.TOO_LARGE as its whole reason, and a parked file read from a cut text says so (reasons.TEXT_CUT). Decision 141: a signed return of the wrong year - a row asks_for_a_return() whose required keywords matched and whose only failure is its period - contests and parks even when another row matched strongly (this year's 1065 with its K-1s, a 1040 with a W-2G stapled behind it); return rows only, checked before the ordinary contested rule. DECISION 140: a read document that reaches the last exit (UNMATCHED) still points somewhere when a row's own form number is shown on the page - a RULE_REQUIRED/RULE_ANY evidence whose term content_check.form_key() reads as a form, said in the title or on the first page (_shows_its_form_number) - or, where no row's is, when the file's name says a row's keyword (_filename_evidence, the unreadable scan's hint): _near_miss() parks it with reasons.SHOWS_ITS_FORM_NUMBER (or, on the name's path, reasons.NAME_POINTS_AT - its own sentence, 'file name', because the page showed nothing) and those rows as the evidence record, NEVER as candidates, so a list where that row is the only one still parks. Only rows whose tier-2 rules let the file through are asked. A01's three required phrases were deliberately not loosened: every looser rule filed the W-3 family and the W-2c as W-2s. The split's self-named forms are self_named, no longer a reuse of the file-name list named.

nodes.role: The unattended pass: for every engagement in the registry, file -> scan -> (on DRAFT_WEEKDAY) draft. This is the whole scheduled task. Decision 130: run_household() refreshes the client README once, after the sort and after every return's scan and draft, still inside the locks (and the README of each household it fed a document into); run_engagement() no longer touches the README.
nodes.notes: Owns the draft-day rule (DRAFT_WEEKDAY) in is_draft_day(); the scheduler does not know about it. One engagement's failure never stops the others, and the run exits non-zero so the scheduler shows red. A drop the filer could not sort marks the engagement failed after the scan and draft still ran. The CLI takes the clients root, not a file; an engagement whose record could not be read fails alone with the reason (RECORD_UNREADABLE), and so does a legacy folder the registry listed. _worth_a_pass() is the pre-checks: skips are not failures, and the warnings the pass reports are manifest.check_rules() over the list the record holds - the same list the app's state carries. Scaffolds each engagement before filing (a row added in the app gets its folder), leaves Override.NOT_APPLICABLE rows out of the outstanding count, and skips an engagement whose successor names it in Rolled From. run_engagement() is the one definition of a pass; the app's scan command calls it too. main(argv) is the command line as a function: python -m tracker.runner and the packaged executable in runner mode (api_entry.py, RUNNER_MODE_FLAG) both call it. Decision 55: should_draft() catches up a draft day the machine missed; an engagement never drafted waits for its first draft day. Decisions 57 and 60: a quiet draft day refreshes the run's own unedited draft (_refresh_stale_draft()) and one a person has edited is never touched. Decision 67: main() makes the console take what it cannot encode before it parses a flag; since decision 108 that guard is page.tolerant_console(), shared by every command line, and main() calls it. Decision 68: append_log() replaces what UTF-8 cannot encode; an engagement's registry warning rides the run's warnings. Decision 69: a FileReport's attention rides the run's warnings, never its error. Decision 75: every real pass ends by writing STATUS_PAGE_FILENAME into the clients root, never on a dry run; status_report() folds the runs just made into every engagement the registry found and reads the rest (no lock, nothing written), so --only and the app's one-engagement pass still draw the whole practice; skipped_because() is the one wording of why an engagement is passed over. Decision 87: the pass gained no call of its own on tracker/ledger.py. Decision 102: run_engagement() holds ONE engagement lock across scaffold, file, scan and view, and tells each step the lock is held; a dry run takes none; a lock it cannot get is a skip. Decision 89: the last thing each engagement's pass does is _view_step(), which regenerates the read-only view; a view whose replace did not land leaves run.view_stale set on a run that still succeeds. Decision 91: write_status_page() is drawn through tracker/page.py. Decision 103: the status page lost its Deferred writes column; nothing a pass decides waits for anything. Decision 104: the pass begins with filer.ensure(), the store's top-up, and nothing in it reads or writes a workbook; the 'Problem or skipped' cell shows the legacy sentence for a folder the tracker no longer reads. Decision 115: _draft_step() runs the gate - a held draft writes nothing, _retire_unedited_drafts() removes the run's own unedited drafts and leaves an edited one, run.held counts the rows and run.draft_note is the refusal (in the console, the log and the practice page's Drafted cell as STATUS_HELD); --reminders always is held too (decision 13 amended). Every draft step ends in _record(): one DRAFTED event through the reminder's record_draft() under the pass's lock, only when something changed or the week's draft is a new week's. last_drafted() answers from the last DRAFTED that wrote a file, and falls back to the files' times for a journal from before 115; draft_is_held() says whether the record's last word is a hold, and should_draft(held=True) drafts on the first pass after the hold clears, first draft or not. Decision 118: a draft a person approved in the app is protected for the rest of that draft week exactly as an edited one is - _draft_step() hands last_draft_day() to write_draft(), _retire_unedited_drafts() and _refresh_stale_draft() as approved_since, EngagementRun carries approved, and _drafted_cell() says APPROVED_NOTE where it would say the stage. The draft day stays the runner's (decision 12): the reminder module is below this one and is handed the week rather than working it out. Decision 129 gave run_household() the registry, so the feed list resolves to this year's returns and the pass takes every lock it needs - its own and the fed ones - in layout.lock_order_key order. A feed that resolves to nothing rides every own return's warnings; a fed return is judged and filed into but never scanned, drafted or drawn here, because that is its own household's pass to make. What the pass filed into a fed return is still this pass's to say, though: one FILED_INTO_FED sentence per fed return that received a filing, on the first own return's warnings, so a household that sorted a drop into somebody else's return does not report 'filed 0' of it. Decision 127: EngagementRun.slowest is the filing report's list of slow readings, and summary() adds SLOW_READING_NOTE for the slowest when it passed SLOW_READING_SECONDS (20.0) - a line the run says, not a limit it enforces; nothing anywhere cuts a reading short, because the benchmark and the owner's speed ceiling are measured in exactly these seconds. In a household the reading is said once, on the first own return's line. Decision 132: A PASS NEEDS THE PRACTICE - run_household()'s registry is required, so Run now and the schedule cannot differ by construction, and a None registry (a root that could not be walked) is refused on every run with NO_PRACTICE and nothing is touched; _feeds_of() says FEEDS_UNREAD on every own return when the household's own record will not read, rather than feeding nothing in silence; _sort_step() hands the sort own= and fed= by name. Decision 131: THE PASS MEASURES BEFORE IT READS - _no_room() runs after _worth_a_pass (which now keeps the loaded list on EngagementRun.items, so the room is measured without a second read) and before the locks: ROOM_PARKS rides the warnings (and the page's Warnings column and the run's lines); a return merely short of room (ROOM_SHORT) is NOT warned (the lead's L-1: names are cut, everything files, and a warning always on is read by nobody) and is still sorted, its names cut to fit; a return whose floor passes the limit skips the WHOLE household with HOUSEHOLD_NO_ROOM, the held-lock shape - nothing read, locked, scaffolded, scanned, drafted or drawn. ONE HOME FOR THE ROOT: main() takes SETTINGS_FLAG (--settings <folder>), sets ENV_SETTINGS_DIR for the process before anything reads settings, and with no root on the command line reads settings.clients_root(); none configured exits naming the settings file and settings.NO_ROOT_HINT (the app first, the command second); a root given by hand still wins - but a root together with --log, the shape of the job installed before 131, is refused with OLD_JOB_ROOT (naming Install Schedule) unless it is the settings file's own root (_refuse_an_old_jobs_root). Decision 137 (L7): main() runs the pass inside content_check.ocr_scratch(settings_dir() / OCR_SCRATCH_DIR_NAME), so OCR's temporary page images land beside the settings file and a killed pass's leftovers are emptied by the next one. Decision 137 Part B: READING_STOP_PAGE_SECONDS and READING_STOP_DOCUMENT_SECONDS are named beside SLOW_READING_SECONDS (the reader, content_check, owns them): a slow reading is named, one past the stop is abandoned. Review fix (F12): main() refuses to walk a saved clients root that clients_root_refusal() refuses.

nodes.role: Turns a return's request list, read from the record, into folders. DECISION 125 - THE HOUSEHOLD'S CLIENT SIDE AND THE RETURN'S FIRM SIDE: scaffold_household() makes the household's folder in the client tree, its one permanent inbox and one folder per open tax year of originals, and lays out folders only (decision 130). DECISION 130 - ONE COMPOSER: write_readme() is the only function that writes the client's _README.txt in that inbox - the steps (README_STEP_2 and README_PHOTO_LINE in Jason's words), REQUESTED, NOT YET RECEIVED per return of the open year (only the requests with no Received line - Jason's decision of 2026-09-23, replacing 124's D-1; NOTHING_OUTSTANDING_LINE when none is left), and WHAT WE HAVE RECEIVED once something has arrived (Received lines per return by request label and day; an Under Review block counted by day, never named) - rendered from a records.Received handed in by tracker.filer.received_for(); it never reads the index (tests/test_layers.py proves it), writes only when the text changed, and with two open years writes nothing, because the pass sorts nothing from an inbox that cannot say which year a document is for. scaffold_engagement() makes the return's Prepared/<folder_name_for(item)>/ plus 00 - Needs Review, and lays out its household too, so a return made on its own still has its inbox and its year folder.
nodes.notes: The folder-name constants it used to own moved to tracker/layout.py with decision 125 - PREPARED_DIR_NAME, REVIEW_DIR_NAME, README_NAME, the two trees and the inbox - and SHARED_DIR_NAME and PBC_DIR_NAME went with the shape they named; this module imports them like everyone else and owns only what it builds (the request list's own file name left with decision 104; there is no such file). Runs on every scheduled pass now, so a row added in the app has its folder by the next run; the README is rewritten only when its text changed. The README contact comes from the engagement's details in the record (firm, else sender) unless given. Decision 61: the README is written whole and a failure to refresh it is a log line, never the end of a pass. Decision 89: the view's own file name lives in tracker/view.py with the module that writes it, as the record's does in tracker/ledger.py - one owner, the writer. Decision 104: it reads through manifest.load_manifest() and manifest.load_engagement_info(), which follow the journal into the store, so it is a reader of tracker.db like every other. Decision 131: the open-year rule (_open_year_of(), read by scaffold_household() and by readme_returns()/write_readme()) retires a prior by discovery's rule - layout.same_return(): the Rolled From path, else its three trailing names - instead of by resolved path only (_resolved is gone), so after the clients root moves a household that has rolled over still reads as one open year and its README is still rewritten. Decision 137 (L6): sanitize_component() never hands back a Windows device name (manifest.WINDOWS_RESERVED_NAMES): it gains a trailing _, so every caller that refuses a changed name refuses it.
